stories.headline: Former Boulder County deputy arrested after shooting at sheriff's headquarters, Broomfield police vehicles with AR-15
stories.summary:
A former Boulder County Sheriff's Office deputy was arrested early Monday morning after allegedly firing multiple shots at the Boulder County Sheriff's Office headquarters in Boulder and at the Broomfield Police Department. Tyler Boyd Reilly, 40, was taken into custody after 1:08 a.m. when deputies confronted him outside the sheriff's headquarters at 5600 Flatiron Parkway, where he had been seen armed with an AR-15-style rifle.

The incident began around 12:02 a.m. when Reilly called 911 reporting anxiety and was transferred to the Westminster Police Department. Minutes later, he called back and made threats against Boulder County Sheriff's facilities before the shootings began. Investigators also determined he had stopped at the Broomfield Police Department, where he is suspected of firing at several police vehicles.

Reilly was arrested without a struggle after deputies confronted him outside the Boulder headquarters. Caution tape blocked the entrance to the facility following the arrest. Charges against Reilly were announced by the Boulder County Sheriff's Office on Monday.

stories.headline: Four Texas homicide suspects arrested in Northglenn after fleeing to Denver metro area
stories.summary:
Four suspects wanted in connection with a Texas homicide were arrested in Northglenn after investigators determined they had fled to the Denver metro area. The primary suspect, identified as Olivo-Olivo, had an arrest warrant issued on Sept. 15 following a targeted shooting in Texas.

Investigators from the U.S. Marshals Service and Homeland Security Investigations in Texas were brought in to help locate the suspects after local detectives established that the shooting was targeted and that multiple individuals were involved. Authorities determined the group had crossed state lines and were believed to be in the greater Denver area.

The U.S. Marshals Service Colorado Violent Offender Task Force ultimately tracked down and arrested the four suspects in Northglenn. The case involved coordination between Texas and Colorado law enforcement agencies, including HSI and the Marshals Service.

stories.headline: Off-duty Pueblo police corporal drowns at Lake Pueblo State Park during wakeboarding accident
stories.summary:
Corporal Stephen Biggs of the Pueblo Police Department drowned Sunday at Lake Pueblo State Park during a wakeboarding accident. Biggs was reported missing at about 5:30 p.m. Sunday, prompting an overnight search involving Colorado Parks and Wildlife, Pueblo County Sheriff's deputies, dive and drone teams, American Medical Response, and Pueblo West Fire.

Biggs' body was recovered at approximately 2 a.m. Monday after he was found submerged in nearly 50 feet of water in the reservoir's main channel, just east of Peck Creek Cove. The accident remains under investigation by Colorado Parks and Wildlife officials.

Biggs had been employed with the Pueblo Police Department since 2010 and was described as an accomplished SWAT officer with 10 letters of commendation, three Medal of Valor awards, and a Distinguished Service award. Pueblo Police Chief Chris Noeller called working with Biggs "an honor" and said his loss is "deeply personal." As a gesture of respect, Biggs' patrol car will be parked in front of the Pueblo Police Department at 200 S. Main St.

stories.headline: Early campaign spending maps Colorado's most contested legislative races ahead of November election
stories.summary:
Independent expenditure committees have begun pouring money into a handful of Colorado state legislative races, offering an early look at the most competitive battlegrounds for the November general election. The Senate Majority Fund, which supports Republican Senate candidates, has spent just over $933,000 on three races through Sept. 16, funded largely by donors including GOPAC, the Republican State Leadership Committee, Occidental Petroleum, and Chevron.

Among the hottest contests is Senate District 30 in Highlands Ranch, where the fund has spent more than $322,000 to defend incumbent Republican Sen. John Carson against Democratic challenger Kevin Leung. Republicans are also targeting Senate District 3 in Pueblo and Senate District 15, which covers parts of Boulder and Larimer counties, in an effort to chip away at the Democrats' 23-12 Senate majority — one seat short of a two-thirds supermajority.

The Senate District 15 race is a rematch between Republican former Sen. Rob Woodward and Democratic incumbent Sen. Janice Marchman, who won the 2022 contest by just over 1,000 votes. The Senate Majority Fund has spent $339,000 so far to back Woodward, while the pro-Democrat All Together Colorado committee has spent nearly $31,000 to support Marchman. House race spending has yet to accelerate significantly but is expected to increase sharply when the next campaign finance report is due Oct. 7.

stories.headline: Colorado Springs Gazette endorses Proposition 86 and Amendment 136 on November ballot
stories.summary:
The Colorado Springs Gazette editorial board has endorsed a "yes" vote on both Proposition 86 and Amendment 136, two measures appearing on Colorado's Nov. 3 mail ballot. Proposition 86 would cap the state's income tax rate at its current 4.4 percent flat rate, acting as a check against Amendment 87, which would replace the flat tax with a tiered bracket system the Gazette characterizes as a roughly $2 billion annual tax increase.

The editorial board argues that Proposition 86 would prevail over Amendment 87's higher-tax provisions even if both measures pass, as long as 86 wins by at least one vote. Amendment 136, meanwhile, would protect the state's independent redistricting commission process from partisan interference, reinforcing a framework Colorado voters approved overwhelmingly in 2018.

Colorado currently has four Democratic and four Republican congressional representatives under its existing district maps, which the Gazette describes as a fair, balanced outcome. The board argues both measures provide structural safeguards for Colorado taxpayers and voters against what it characterizes as threats to fiscal discipline and political independence.

stories.headline: Major flooding threat looms for Colorado as remnants of Hurricane Polo merge with Pacific storm system
stories.summary:
Colorado is facing its most significant rainfall event in more than three years this week as the remnants of Hurricane Polo merge with a Pacific low-pressure system and drive a surge of tropical moisture into the state. Denver7's weather team has issued a Weather Impact Alert for Wednesday, when the heaviest rain is expected to strike the Front Range, with up to an inch of rainfall possible in some Denver-area locations.

A Flood Watch is in effect for the Palmer Divide and nearby plains, including parts of Elbert and Lincoln counties, from Tuesday evening through Thursday morning. The southeastern Denver metro could see 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain, with locally 3 to 4 inches possible across the southern tier of the state. Slow-moving, repeated rounds of moderate rain over the same areas raise the risk of flash flooding, particularly in low-lying and poor-drainage zones.

Temperatures will drop well below normal through Thursday, with highs holding in the mid-to-upper 60s along the Interstate 25 corridor. A mix of snow is possible at mountain elevations above roughly 11,000 feet if temperatures cool sufficiently. Conditions are expected to improve by Friday, with warmer and drier weather returning through the weekend.

stories.headline: RTD light rail train strikes and injures person in Denver metro
stories.summary:
An RTD light rail train struck and injured a person in the Denver metro area on Saturday night, according to reporting from the Denver Post. Details on the victim's condition and the specific location of the incident were not immediately available.

The incident adds to ongoing safety concerns surrounding the regional light rail network. RTD has faced scrutiny in recent years over pedestrian and vehicle safety at and near rail crossings across the Denver metro system.

stories.headline: Vape shop chain reaches settlement with Colorado over illegal kratom sales
stories.summary:
The owners of a Colorado vape shop chain have reached a settlement with the state after being accused of selling illegal kratom products in their stores. The Colorado attorney general's office had accused the chain of violating state law by stocking kratom, a botanical substance that has drawn scrutiny from health officials and regulators.

The settlement terms were not fully detailed in available reporting. The action comes amid growing concern in Colorado over kratom availability, particularly following warnings from health officials about rising use of the substance among teenagers.

stories.headline: Talanoa Hufanga's pick-6 off Stafford breaks NFL record, lifts Broncos to 30-26 win over Rams
stories.summary:
Denver Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga delivered one of the most consequential plays of the young NFL season Sunday night, intercepting Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford and returning the ball 66 yards for a touchdown that broke an NFL record and swung the game in Denver's favor. Stafford's pass to running back Kyren Williams, who split out wide on a third down, went slightly off-target, allowing Hufanga to step in front of it for the pick-6. The interception made Stafford the NFL's all-time leader in touchdown passes thrown to the opposing team, surpassing Brett Favre.

The play capped a stunning comeback in which the Broncos scored 30 points over a 22-minute span after going scoreless for more than 37 minutes. Denver trailed 19-16 when the interception occurred, and the defense held on as the Rams made one final attempt to respond. The win improved the Broncos' record in one-score games to 13-2 since the start of the 2025 season.

Head coach Sean Payton acknowledged the team's persistent pattern of slow starts and explosive finishes, saying he is "comfortable with the grit" of a team that wins in the fourth quarter but "uncomfortable" with how the Broncos play early. Denver has scored just 10 points in three first halves this season compared to 50 points in three second halves. Payton indicated the team must correct its early-game struggles to remain a serious Super Bowl contender.

stories.headline: Avalanche release full roster breakdown ahead of Wednesday's season opener against Kings
stories.summary:
The Colorado Avalanche open the 2026-27 NHL season Wednesday night at Ball Arena against the Los Angeles Kings, with a roster finalized under deadline pressure after the league's Monday submission cutoff. The team will carry a rookie in its opening-night lineup, with undrafted forward T.J. Hughes earning a spot after a strong training camp and a productive stint in the Calder Cup Playoffs.

Nathan MacKinnon enters the season with a chance to become the fifth player in NHL history to record five consecutive seasons of 110 or more points, joining Wayne Gretzky, Mike Bossy, Guy Lafleur, and Phil Esposito in that group. Defenseman Cale Makar is described as fully healthy heading into the season opener, a significant development after health questions lingered through the offseason.

The Avalanche are navigating key roster questions, including how newly acquired center Nazem Kadri, who turns 37 next week, fits into the top-six forward group, and whether Martin Necas can deliver a strong postseason after signing an $11.5 million annual deal. Forward Aatu Raty is starting the season on injured reserve. The team is seeking to improve on a record-setting regular season that ended in another disappointing playoff exit.

stories.headline: Former Avalanche defenseman Erik Johnson lists Cherry Hills Village mansion for $14.5 million
stories.summary:
Erik Johnson, the former Colorado Avalanche defenseman who recently transitioned to broadcasting after signing with ESPN as an NHL analyst, has listed his Cherry Hills Village home for $14.5 million. The listing marks the end of Johnson's residential chapter in the Denver metro area following a lengthy career with the Avalanche.

Johnson was a fixture in the Colorado lineup for more than a decade and was a key piece of the franchise's 2022 Stanley Cup championship team. The Cherry Hills Village property reflects the high-end residential market in one of the Denver metro's most exclusive communities.

stories.headline: Data center opposition tour stops in Colorado Springs amid ongoing debate over Project Taurus
stories.summary:
A national bus tour opposing data center developments made a stop in Colorado Springs as local public debate continues over Project Taurus, a proposed facility near Garden of the Gods Road. The tour's arrival highlights growing grassroots resistance to large-scale data center construction in communities concerned about land use, water consumption, and energy demands.

Project Taurus has drawn scrutiny from residents and local officials in Colorado Springs, with concerns centering on its proximity to the Garden of the Gods area, one of the city's most prominent natural landmarks. The national tour's stop in Colorado Springs signals the local fight has attracted broader attention from advocacy groups tracking data center expansion across the country.

topStory.headline: Trump Vows Victory Over Iran 'One Way or Another' as Ceasefire Talks Stall and Strait of Hormuz Attack Reported
topStory.summary:
President Donald Trump declared the United States would prevail against Iran "one way or another" and predicted the conflict would be resolved "pretty quickly," even as diplomatic efforts appeared to be faltering. Trump confirmed that U.S. negotiators had spoken with Iranian officials through mediators, but rejected Tehran's latest ceasefire proposal, while Iran's government said it has "no plans" to negotiate directly with Washington.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, speaking to reporters in New York on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, insisted Tehran had made no changes to its seven-point ceasefire proposal, which calls for a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the U.S. meeting conditions outlined in a memorandum of understanding signed in June. Araghchi said Iran had conveyed the plan through Qatari intermediaries and was still awaiting a formal American response. Iranian government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani separately accused the U.S. of "bullying" over air sanctions, saying Tehran had filed a complaint with the International Civil Aviation Organization.

A vessel was struck by a suspected projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz late Monday, according to the U.K. Navy's Maritime Trade Operations center. The fire aboard the ship was extinguished and the crew was reported safe, though no country claimed responsibility for the strike. The incident is among the latest in a series of attacks on vessels using the waterway, which connects Persian Gulf energy producers to international markets.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced Tuesday it is developing new weapons to defend the country, while the value of Iran's currency fell to a new record low, with traders in Tehran exchanging more than 2.5 million rials for a single U.S. dollar. That figure marked a further decline from the previous record of 2.4 million rials to the dollar set just one day earlier, underscoring the mounting economic toll of the conflict on the Iranian population and government. The IRGC's weapons announcement signals Iran is preparing for a range of military contingencies even as diplomatic channels remain nominally open.

The breakdown in direct negotiations raises the risk of further escalation in a conflict that has already disrupted global shipping through one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints. With Trump ruling out Iran's ceasefire terms and Tehran refusing direct talks, the path to a negotiated resolution remains unclear. The situation continues to reverberate in global markets, with Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers citing Middle East instability as a key driver of inflation pressures in his country.
